page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL40S is a KVM-based GPU-accelerated server. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F x86_64 processor with 12 vCPUs consisting of 12 physical cores and 1 thread per core under a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Hardware acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, featuring 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing. Multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls in the average tier, reflecting the 12-core configuration. Large-block memory bandwidth is strong, while small-block cached read bandwidth remains average. For LLM inference, the server achieves top-tier generation speeds with small 135M models and strong generation speeds with medium 7B models, though prompt processing and larger 70B model execution scale down to average tiers.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for GPU-accelerated workloads requiring substantial VRAM relative to a moderate 12-vCPU compute footprint. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete lack of local storage, requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is highly suited for machine learning inference, medium-scale LLM execution, image processing, and GPU-accelerated data science tasks.
description: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL40S is a KVM-based GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-intensive and machine learning workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F x86_64 processor with 12 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory. Graphics and parallel processing are driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. While the server lacks local storage, it delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong large-block memory bandwidth. Benchmark results highlight top-tier text generation speeds for small LLMs and strong performance for medium models. The high VRAM-to-vCPU ratio makes this instance qualitatively cost-efficient for specialized workloads such as AI inference, image processing, and GPU-accelerated data science, though users must account for the shared CPU allocation and external storage requirements.
